newsitem.title: USA: First Lady, Powell join to advocate volunteerism.
newsitem.headline: First Lady, Powell join to advocate volunteerism.

text.p: First lady Hillary Rodham Clinton, retired Gen. Colin Powell and television talk-show host Oprah Winfrey joined forces Wednesday to highlight the need for volunteerism to help children.
The three participated in a videoconference that was a prelude to The Presidents' Summit For America's Future, which is scheduled for April 27-29 in Philadelphia.

President Clinton and former President George Bush are expected to attend the summit which will bring together community representatives from around the country to discuss how to increase help for children through volunteer mentors, tutors and other services.
"Throughout this month the Clinton Administration will be highlighting the importance of citizen service," Mrs. Clinton said.
"No task facing America is more crucial or more difficult than the task of preparing our children for the future," she added.
Powell said a goal was to cross racial and ethnic lines.
"Make sure you reach out to a youngster that doesn't look like you, a youngster that perhaps doesn't dress like you," Powell said.
